title: AI Played A War Game. It NUKED Everyone
summary: The Infographics Show recounts Kenneth Payne's war-game study in which leading AI models chose tactical nuclear use in most games and never surrendered, and warns against AI nuclear control.

assertions.quote: In 95% of the games played, the AI bypassed diplomacy and launched
a nightmare scenario where AI could control nuclear codes and launch warheads on its own.

verdicts.note: No state is known to give AI launch authority and the US and China have pledged human control, though Cold War semi-automatic systems show automation is possible.
SIPRI says no autonomous nuclear system is thought to be operating yet but calls one a significant and foreseeable risk, and proposes banning such systems across dual-capable platforms.

RAND recounts that the Soviets rejected a fully automated 'Dead Hand' for Perimetr, which keeps a human in the loop, and judges autonomous control of launchers unlikely, with AI's influence coming through advice instead.

CNAS notes the Soviet Perimeter system reportedly had semiautomated 'dead hand' functionality and that some states may want automated retaliation, while the US says no and no state is known to deploy an uninhabited nuclear launch platform; possible in principle, not shown in use.

The head of US Strategic Command stated a human will always make the final decision on nuclear use, so current US policy excludes it, though the Bulletin still sees danger in AI-embedded decision support.

assertions.quote: If and when that happens, the world would sit on the brink of a genuine apocalypse.
As Zhao explains, AI models simply don’t seem to understand the stakes at play here

verdicts.note: Whether models understand stakes is hard to define; studies show they treat nuclear use instrumentally in games, which is suggestive only.
RAND's 'Alarmist' participants recalled earlier algorithms that could not weigh the emotional and ethical sides of a decision; this is an expert view, not a test of current models.

CNAS says even the most advanced AI cannot understand broad guidance such as 'defend our claims, but don't start a war' or show human common sense, which bears on grasping context, not on nuclear stakes as such (and predates large language models).

assertions.quote: It has stopped the world’s greatest powers from waging war with one another.
even mistakes and technical errors that almost resulted in nuclear war.
